title: Oh Hell with more chaos. My solo card game just got a major visual overhaul
author: estist
selftext:
I have been working on an Android card game called Oh Fudge, based on Oh Hell. I am a solo developer and have been using AI to help me build something I would never have the art or coding skills to make on my own.

One of the biggest problems I had was the graphics. Visual 1.0 was basically me making things as I needed them. I would get an idea, work with AI to make it, like it, and put it in the game. The problem was after doing that for a while I had a bunch of graphics I liked, but they didn't look like they came from the same game. Different styles, different detail, different characters and just no real visual identity.

So ChatGPT and I started Visual 2.0.

That turned into way more work than I expected. We worked through what the game should actually look and feel like, colors, UI, backgrounds, characters, the Joker, playing cards and all the little things that make everything feel like it belongs together. There was a lot of making an image, finding what was wrong, changing it, going too far, trying to go back, watching the style slowly drift away, throwing it out and starting over.

The biggest thing I learned was that getting one good AI image isn't that hard. Getting 100 different images made at different times that all look like they belong in the same game is a whole different problem.

We ended up making a strict Visual 2.0 setup with master references and rules for how things should look. One of the biggest rules is when an image starts drifting too far, stop using that image as the reference. Go back to the original 2.0 references and start again. That has helped a ton with keeping the Joker looking like the same Joker and keeping the whole game from slowly turning into a bunch of different AI art styles again.

Now I am taking all of that work into Claude on the coding side. I am replacing the old graphics, changing screens to work with the new ones, adding new animations and effects, and trying to make the actual game feel like Visual 2.0 instead of just putting new pictures on top of Visual 1.0.

It has honestly been a pain sometimes, but I have learned a ton doing it. AI didn't just spit out Visual 2.0 for me. It has been a lot of me telling it what I want, figuring out why something doesn't work, rejecting stuff, starting over and slowly building rules that keep everything together.

Visual 1.0 looked like a solo developer grabbing whatever he could make and putting a game together.

My goal with Visual 2.0 is for you to just look at it and think, yeah, all of this belongs in Oh Fudge.

If you like trick taking games, come check it out and let me know what you think!
